Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, inspect the rollout evidence—including both required wake views—and consult the fish-control bookshelf before proposing or editing the policy. Then I’ll implement exactly one candidate and update both required documentation files with evidence-backed conclusions.

I’m applying two workspace skills now: `read-wake-visual-signals-first` sets the required visual inspection order, and `fish-control-primitives` governs how any external mechanism may be translated into the two-joint controller. Their constraints will shape the candidate and the notes.

The sampled set contains four direct-uniform still-water captures, so there is no termination failure to compare. I’m treating the slower v49 rollout as the informative comparative failure and the reproduced v50 rollout as the strongest finite result; I’ll also inspect v52 because it tests a distinct terminal-slip mechanism.

The evidence isolates a concrete failure mode: v52’s direct terminal course-slip curvature improved lateral alignment slightly but did not advance capture and made the terminal crossing shallower, while increasing actuator-limit residence. I’m recording a single alternative hypothesis before editing: feed the same normalized course signal into the existing bounded desired-yaw-rate loop, so observed yaw response arbitrates it, instead of stacking another direct route-curvature term.

The candidate now compiles and returns finite bounded two-joint accelerations. I’m checking its behavioral locality next: exact equivalence to v50 outside approach and without positive closure, reflection symmetry, and frozen-trace support. This is a contract/localization check only—no CFD will be run.

The frozen v50 trace confirms the response gate is doing what the direct v52 term did not: it is exactly inactive outside `2.1 L` and without positive closure, and at capture it suppresses 99.5% of the course request because de-gaited yaw is already correcting in the requested direction. I’m now distilling the completed v52 result—not the unevaluated candidate—into reusable guidance.

The first mandated guidance check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` marks the same optimizer parent twice, so provenance cannot be resolved. I’m removing only the duplicated parent line—the same repair documented in the sampled v52 worker—then rerunning the check.

The candidate and both required evidence files are now complete. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated no-CFD check runner on the finalized workspace; if its pinned model is unavailable, I’ll retain the already completed local equivalents and report that infrastructure limitation explicitly.

The dedicated runner was invoked but could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unsupported on this ChatGPT account. I’m rerunning its exact checks locally on the finalized files and will record that distinction; this remains no-CFD validation.

Produced exactly one candidate: `dogfish_target_control_v53_response_arbitrated_terminal_course`.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:7) — bounded terminal course feedback routed through the existing yaw-response loop. SHA-256: `d65a9dc5…eae70`.
- [Candidate notes](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) — visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer block, falsification criteria, and audit.
- [Reusable guidance](guidance/control_experience.md:284) — records the negative v52 direct-course result and response-arbitration boundary.

All three exact no-CFD checks pass locally, including the 69-reference/71-field schema guard. The configured checker was invoked but its pinned model is unsupported on this account. No CFD was run.
